note: Two primitive camping spots at Pin Oak Lake, in open prairie. The main one is a mown point of about 45 by 55 m on the lake's west shore, reached by a short two-track off the gravel road to the boat ramp and fishing dock; the other is a small gravel turnaround loop on SW 50th Road below the dam, where the embankment hides the lake. No pads, tables or toilets. MDC calls the campsites best suited to tents and small travel trailers or RVs. Electric motors only on the lake. --Claude
summary: Confirmed as designated drive-in camping: two mapped primitive camps at Pin Oak Lake (area page, brochure, map symbols, two GIS points). Pin is on the minor roadside loop; PIN MOVE proposed to the lake-point camp 360 m north-west. Waterfront lead UP to lakefront at that camp. MDC wording 'small travel trailers/RVs' flagged as a caveat. Phone matches.
flags: PIN MOVE (minor spot -> main camp): stored 37.43488,-94.56622 is GIS point 634 ('Designated Camping Area') with lot 3674 14 m away: a gravel turnaround loop about 25 m across around one tree, directly off SW 50th Road, at the outside foot of Pin Oak Lake's dam. The other GIS point, 420 ('Primitive Camping Area') at 37.43738,-94.56882, is 360 m north-west on the same lake road: a mown knoll roughly 45 x 55 m on a point of the west shore with a faint two-track running up its middle from the gravel road to the boat ramp. It is the larger and plainly the better camp. Proposed pin 37.43738,-94.56882. Both are on the map as Primitive Camping symbols at Pin Oak Lake; the two are 360 m apart on one road system, so no split.

WATERFRONT LEAD UP (stored not waterfront, no stored evidence): at the lake-point camp the mown ground runs to the shore on the east and north sides: on the 0.14 m/px frame the two-track is about 25 m from the east shore and the north end of the mown knoll is 10-15 m from the water, with only mown grass and a narrow reed fringe between. No road, lot or day use between (the ramp lot is to the south-east). Pin Oak Lake measures about 400 m long and 100-130 m wide on the frame - roughly 10-12 acres as an imagery estimate (Overpass timed out; MDC publishes no acreage), so it is over the 5-acre pond line. Supports LAKEFRONT if the pin moves to that camp. At the stored pin (roadside loop) the dam embankment stands between the loop and the water about 30 m away: not waterfront there.

CRITERIA / RIG WORDING (caveat, not a drop): the area page says 'Camping is allowed at the designated campsites near Pin Oak Lake. Tent camping and small travel trailers/RVs are best suited for these campsites. All campsites are primitive and are on a first come-first served basis.' No length is stated. This wording is specific to this area (not MDC boilerplate). On imagery both spots are open and level-looking with a gravel county road and gravel lake road to them, nothing that would stop a 23-ft motorhome: the roadside loop is a ~25 m turnaround, and the lake camp is open mown ground entered by a two-track (grass, no pad - soft when wet). I did not search for a dated camper report of a 23-ft+ rig here. Proposed note carries the MDC wording.

INCLUSION (stays): brochure: 'Primitive camping is permitted at the designated camping areas (see area map). Campers are limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period.' and 'No open fires except in designated camping areas.' No special-use-permit rule for camping (trapping and field trials only), no Rule 101, no 'camping is prohibited' line. Things to Do: Camping - Individual Campsites. No low-water crossing or 4WD wording; access is Route M and gravel SW 50th Road.
